opciones.texto: It shows a strong conclusion from evidence.
It gives the cloud an obligation.

opcion_multiple.feedback_correcto: Exactly. Sentence A reports; sentence B reconstructs the event from clues.
opcion_multiple.feedback_incorrecto: No one witnessed the event, and no one is giving an order. Sentence B is a conclusion built from evidence.

display.headline: What does the speaker actually know?
display.body: Las dos frases apuntan al mismo evento, pero no hacen la misma afirmación.

comparison.right: The cloud must have replaced the file.

audio.text: Look at the two sentences. They describe the same event, but they do not express the same certainty. What changes in sentence B?

instruccion.texto: Must marks a strong deduction. Might or could leaves a possibility open. Can't rules it out. To aim the deduction at the past, add have, then the past participle.

display.headline: One past. Three levels of confidence.
display.body: El modal calibra tu certeza. HAVE mueve esa deducción hacia un hecho pasado.

concepts.example: The cloud must have replaced it.

audio.text: Use ‘must have’ for a strong deduction about the past. Use ‘might have’ or ‘could have’ to keep a possibility open. Use ‘can’t have’ when the evidence rules something out. The pattern is: modal, have, past participle.

opcion_multiple.pregunta: The edit log names Camila as the author. Camila ___ changed the title.
opcion_multiple.feedback_correcto: The log names her. The evidence supports the strongest deduction: must have.
opcion_multiple.feedback_incorrecto: The log directly names Camila. Use the strongest deduction the clue earns.

display.headline: How strong is the evidence?
display.body: No elijas la forma más segura: elige la fuerza que la pista realmente permite.
